title: Variables, Expressions & Memory Model
learning_objectives: Trace variable assignment as name tags bound to heap objects using id()

learning_objectives: Utilize math functions and sys parameters for algorithmic utility

description: Compute tree height, diameter, balance factors, and test tree symmetry using bottom-up post-order DFS in O(N) time.

title: Binary Search Tree (BST) Invariant & Search
learning_objectives: Verify binary search tree validity by passing recursive open interval bounds (low, high)
Search for target keys in O(H) time where H is tree height
description: Understand the BST property (Left < Root < Right), validate BST invariants, and perform O(H) key lookups.

title: BST Insertion, Deletion & Successor Rewiring
learning_objectives: Insert new values into BST leaf positions preserving the BST invariant
Delete interior nodes with two children by substituting the in-order successor
description: Implement BST insertion and deletion, handling 0, 1, and 2-child cases and in-order successor replacements.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) in BST and Tree
learning_objectives: Find the LCA of two nodes in a BST in O(H) time using numerical value bifurcation
Locate LCA in general binary trees using post-order node presence bubbling
description: Find the Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) in BSTs in O(H) time and general binary trees in O(N) time via DFS.

title: Tree Serialization & Deserialization
learning_objectives: Encode a binary tree into a delimited string representation using pre-order traversal with null markers
Reconstruct the identical tree structure from string tokens in O(N) time
description: Serialize binary trees into flat string representations and reconstruct them using pre-order and BFS iterators.

title: Morris In-Order Traversal & Threaded Pointers
learning_objectives: Establish temporary threads from in-order predecessors to current nodes
Traverse binary search trees in strictly O(1) auxiliary space without stack or recursion
description: Traverse binary trees in-order in O(1) auxiliary space using Morris Traversal and threaded binary tree pointers.

title: Balanced BSTs: AVL Tree Rotations (LL, RR)
concepts: Single & Double Rotations (LL, RR, LR, RL)
learning_objectives: Calculate AVL node balance factors from left and right subtree heights
Trace single and double tree rotations that restore O(log N) height balance
description: Understand AVL balance factors, height-balance invariants, and implement left and right tree rotations.

title: Red-Black Tree Principles & Invariants
learning_objectives: Trace the 5 Red-Black tree properties guaranteeing maximum height <= 2 log(N+1)
Differentiate recoloring steps from rotation steps during node insertion
description: Analyze Red-Black tree color invariants, black-height guarantees, and compare performance trade-offs against AVL trees.

title: Tries (Prefix Trees): Structure & Lookup
learning_objectives: Implement a prefix Trie with insert, search, and startsWith methods in O(L) time
Contrast Trie string prefix search with hash map string lookups
description: Build a Trie (Prefix Tree) data structure supporting O(L) word insertion, full-word search, and prefix matching.

title: Trie Applications: Autocomplete & Wildcards
learning_objectives: Implement an autocomplete search engine returning all words sharing a common prefix
Traverse all child branches upon encountering wildcard '.' characters
description: Apply Tries to autocomplete dictionary queries and wildcard pattern searches using recursive backtracking.

title: Section 9 Review & Tree Recursion Mastery
learning_objectives: Architect an in-memory search catalog combining a Trie with a balanced BST
Evaluate asymptotic worst-case bounds on degenerate vs balanced trees
description: Synthesize binary tree recursions, BST search invariants, self-balancing rotations, and prefix Trie indexing.

title: Binary Heap Layout in Flat Arrays
learning_objectives: Map a complete binary tree into a 1D flat array using parent=(i-1)//2 and children=2i+1, 2i+2
Verify the binary min-heap property: parent <= children
description: Examine binary heap flat-array indexing (parent = (i-1)//2, left = 2i+1, right = 2i+2) and complete tree layouts.

title: Heapify, Sift-Up & Sift-Down Mechanics
learning_objectives: Implement sift-up and sift-down mechanics to restore heap invariants in O(log N) time
Prove mathematically that bottom-up heapify builds a heap in linear O(N) time
description: Implement sift-up and sift-down operations, and prove that bottom-up heapify runs in linear O(N) time.

title: Python's heapq Module & Tie-Breaker Patterns
learning_objectives: Use heapq.heappush, heappop, and heapify to manage priority queues
Prevent tuple comparison crashes on identical priorities using unique counter sequence ids
description: Master Python's heapq module, simulate max-heaps via negation, and use counter tie-breakers to prevent comparison crashes.

title: Top K Frequent Elements in Data Streams
learning_objectives: Maintain a min-heap of size K to identify top K frequent elements in O(N log K) time
Contrast bounded min-heap filtering against full O(N log N) array sorting
description: Find the K most frequent items in continuous streams in O(N log K) time using bounded min-heaps.

title: Merge K Sorted Lists via Min-Heap
learning_objectives: Merge K sorted linked lists or streams using a min-heap tracking current heads
Achieve optimal O(N log K) total runtime and O(K) auxiliary space
description: Merge K sorted lists or streams into a single sorted list in O(N log K) time using priority queue frontiers.

title: Two-Heap Pattern: Median of a Stream
learning_objectives: Balance a max-heap of smaller elements and min-heap of larger elements
Retrieve running medians in O(1) time and insert stream values in O(log N) time
description: Implement the two-heap pattern (max-heap for lower half, min-heap for upper half) to find stream medians in O(1) time.

title: Task Scheduler & Priority Reorganization
learning_objectives: Schedule CPU tasks with cooldown interval n using a max-heap and wait queue
Compute minimum CPU idle intervals to complete all tasks
description: Schedule CPU tasks with cooling intervals using greedy max-heaps and cooldown queue staging in O(N) time.

title: Indexed Priority Queue Principles
learning_objectives: Augment a binary heap with a hash map tracking element array indices
Update priorities in-place (decrease_key) in strict O(log N) time without scanning
description: Design an Indexed Priority Queue supporting O(log N) arbitrary priority updates (decrease-key) and deletions.

title: Kth Smallest Element in Sorted Matrix
learning_objectives: Extract K smallest elements from row-and-column sorted matrices via frontier heaps
Contrast priority queue frontier search against monotonic binary search
description: Locate the Kth smallest element in row/column sorted matrices using heap frontier exploration in O(K log N) time.

title: Section 10 Review & Priority Queue Design
learning_objectives: Architect a priority dispatch engine handling dynamic priority shifts and task starvation
Evaluate space-time trade-offs between two-heaps, sorted arrays, and balanced BSTs
description: Synthesize binary heap algorithms, running median dual-heaps, and indexed priority queues into a streaming scheduler.

title: Graph Representations & Adjacency Lists
learning_objectives: Construct adjacency list dictionary representations from edge lists in O(V + E) time
Evaluate space and edge query trade-offs between sparse lists and dense matrices
description: Represent graphs using adjacency lists, adjacency matrices, and edge lists; evaluate density trade-offs.

title: BFS & Unweighted Shortest Path
learning_objectives: Implement Breadth-First Search (BFS) to find shortest path distances on unweighted graphs
Reconstruct shortest path vertices using a predecessor parent map in O(V + E) time
description: Implement BFS using collections.deque to find shortest paths on unweighted graphs and reconstruct shortest paths.

title: DFS, Connected Components & Flood Fill
learning_objectives: Traverse all reachable graph vertices using Depth-First Search with a visited set
Count connected components and solve 2D grid flood fill problems in O(V + E) time
description: Implement recursive and iterative DFS, count connected components, and solve 2D grid flood fill problems.

title: Cycle Detection in Directed Graphs (3-Color)
learning_objectives: Detect cycles in directed graphs by identifying back-edges to gray nodes on the current recursion stack
Differentiate directed cycle detection from undirected visited-set checks
description: Detect cycles in directed graphs using three-color DFS marking (Unvisited, Visiting, Visited) and back-edge identification.

title: Topological Sort: Kahn's In-Degree BFS
learning_objectives: Compute vertex in-degrees and process zero-in-degree nodes sequentially
Produce a valid topological order of a DAG or detect cyclic dependency errors in O(V + E) time
description: Implement Kahn's algorithm for topological sorting of DAGs using in-degree arrays and zero-degree queues.

title: Topological Sort: DFS Post-Order Reversal
learning_objectives: Record DFS finish order and reverse the post-order sequence to produce a topological sort
Solve Course Schedule II under prerequisite constraints
description: Implement topological sort using DFS post-order traversal reversal and detect invalid cyclic dependencies.

title: Bipartite Graph Verification (2-Coloring)
learning_objectives: Color graph vertices with two alternating labels using BFS/DFS
Prove a graph is non-bipartite if adjacent vertices share identical color labels
description: Determine whether a graph is bipartite (2-colorable) using alternating BFS/DFS vertex coloring in O(V + E) time.

title: Dijkstra's Algorithm: Shortest Paths
learning_objectives: Implement Dijkstra's algorithm to compute single-source shortest paths on non-negative weighted graphs
Maintain a min-heap of tentative distances and skip stale extracted entries in O((V + E) log V) time
description: Implement Dijkstra's algorithm using priority queues to compute single-source shortest paths with non-negative edge weights.

title: Bellman-Ford & Negative Cycle Detection
concepts: Negative Weight Cycle Detection on Pass V
learning_objectives: Relax all graph edges V - 1 times to find shortest paths with negative edge weights
Identify negative-weight cycles by checking if distances continue decreasing on pass V
description: Implement the Bellman-Ford algorithm in O(V * E) time, handle negative weights, and detect reachable negative cycles.

title: Disjoint Set Union (DSU / Union-Find)
concepts: Union by Rank/Size & Inverse Ackermann O(alpha(N))
learning_objectives: Implement Disjoint Set Union (Union-Find) with root representative find operations
Achieve nearly O(1) amortized operations using Path Compression and Union by Rank
description: Implement Disjoint Set Union (DSU) with Path Compression and Union by Rank, achieving near-O(1) amortized time.

title: Minimum Spanning Tree: Kruskal's with DSU
learning_objectives: Sort all graph edges by weight and greedily select non-cyclic edges using DSU
Construct a Minimum Spanning Tree in O(E log E) time
description: Implement Kruskal's algorithm to find Minimum Spanning Trees (MST) by sorting edges and avoiding cycles with DSU.

title: Minimum Spanning Tree: Prim's Algorithm
learning_objectives: Grow an MST from a start vertex by repeatedly selecting the minimum crossing edge via a min-heap
Achieve O((V + E) log V) runtime on dense graphs
description: Implement Prim's algorithm for Minimum Spanning Trees using priority queues to select minimum crossing edges.

title: Undirected Bridges & Articulation Points
learning_objectives: Calculate discovery times and lowest reachable ancestor depths during a single DFS traversal
Locate all critical bridges and articulation cut-vertices in O(V + E) time
description: Find all bridges and articulation points in undirected graphs using Tarjan's discovery time (tin) and low-link (low) DFS.

title: Strongly Connected Components (Kosaraju)
learning_objectives: Reconstruct transposed reversed graphs where directed edge orientations are inverted
Extract all Strongly Connected Components (SCCs) in directed graphs using Kosaraju's algorithm in O(V + E) time
description: Implement Kosaraju's two-pass DFS algorithm on graphs and their transposes to find Strongly Connected Components in DAGs.

title: Section 11 Review & Graph Synthesis
learning_objectives: Design a multi-modal routing engine integrating Dijkstra, BFS, and DSU under real-world constraints
Condense directed cyclic graphs into topological DAG components
description: Synthesize BFS, DFS, topological sorting, Dijkstra, DSU, MSTs, and SCC algorithms into a comprehensive network router.

title: Greedy Choice Property & Exchange Arguments
learning_objectives: Evaluate whether locally optimal choices lead to globally optimal solutions
Formulate exchange argument proofs showing no optimal solution beats greedy
description: Understand the Greedy Choice Property, Optimal Substructure, and prove optimality using exchange arguments.

title: Activity Selection & Interval Scheduling
learning_objectives: Sort intervals by earliest finish time to maximize non-overlapping scheduled tasks
Prove greedy interval scheduling optimality in O(N log N) time
description: Solve the Activity Selection problem by sorting on earliest finish time, proving optimality via exchange arguments.

title: Fractional Knapsack & Value Density Sorting
learning_objectives: Sort items by value-per-weight density to maximize total value in fractional knapsacks
Contrast fractional greedy solvability with 0/1 integer knapsack NP-hardness
description: Implement the Fractional Knapsack problem in O(N log N) time by greedily sorting items by value-to-weight density.

title: Huffman Coding & Optimal Prefix Trees
learning_objectives: Construct an optimal prefix code tree by repeatedly merging the two least frequent nodes
Generate variable-length binary encoding tables without prefix ambiguity
description: Construct optimal variable-length prefix codes using Huffman's algorithm with priority queues in O(N log N) time.

title: Jump Game & Reachability Frontiers
learning_objectives: Track maximum reachable index frontiers to determine if array ends are reachable in O(N) time
Compute minimum jumps to reach the end using greedy interval boundary shifts
description: Solve Jump Game I (reachability) and Jump Game II (minimum jumps) using greedy frontier advancement in O(N) time.

title: Partition Labels & Last Seen Indices
learning_objectives: Record the last occurrence index of each character to partition strings into disjoint subsegments
Return maximum partition sizes in O(N) time and O(1) space
description: Partition strings into maximal parts such that each character appears in at most one part in O(N) time.

title: Gas Station & Circular Circuit Greedy
learning_objectives: Prove a unique starting gas station exists if and only if total gas >= total cost
Reset prospective starting points in a single O(N) scan whenever running tank deficits occur
description: Determine the starting gas station to complete a circular tour in O(N) time using net balance greedy sweeps.

title: Candy Distribution: Two-Pass Greedy
learning_objectives: Satisfy neighbor rating constraints using independent forward and backward greedy sweeps
Compute minimum required resources in O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space
description: Solve the Candy distribution problem using two independent greedy passes (left-to-right, right-to-left) in O(N) time.

title: Frequency Decrementing for Uniqueness
learning_objectives: Ensure all character frequencies are strictly unique by greedily decrementing duplicates
Compute minimum character deletions in O(N) time and O(K) space
description: Find the minimum character deletions to make all character frequencies unique using greedy decrement sets.

title: Section 12 Review & Greedy Proof Formalism
learning_objectives: Determine whether optimization problems admit greedy solutions or require dynamic programming
Implement job sequencing with deadlines and profits using greedy selection and DSU
description: Synthesize greedy choice proofs, interval scheduling, reachability frontiers, and distinguish greedy from DP.

title: Memoization vs Tabulation Paradigms
learning_objectives: Identify overlapping subproblems in recursive DAGs and cache results in hash maps
Construct iterative bottom-up tables eliminating call stack overhead
description: Understand overlapping subproblems, optimal substructure, top-down memoization (lru_cache) vs bottom-up tabulation.

title: 1D DP: Climbing Stairs & House Robber
learning_objectives: Formulate 1D state transition equations dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + val)
Compress 1D DP arrays into two rolling variables achieving O(1) auxiliary space
description: Formulate 1D DP recurrences (Climbing Stairs, House Robber) and optimize auxiliary space to O(1) rolling variables.

title: 2D Grid DP: Unique Paths & Min Path Sum
learning_objectives: Compute unique paths and minimum path sums on grids with obstacles
Optimize 2D grid DP memory from O(M * N) to O(N) single-row buffers
description: Solve grid dynamic programming problems (Unique Paths, Minimum Path Sum) and compress 2D tables into 1D rows in O(M*N) time.

title: 0/1 Knapsack: Table to 1D Reverse Pass
concepts: 1D Reverse Traversal to Prevent Item Re-use
learning_objectives: Formulate the 0/1 Knapsack recurrence choosing to include or skip current item
Debug 1D space-optimized knapsack updates by reversing capacity sweeps from W down to weight
description: Master the classical 0/1 Knapsack problem, formulate 2D state tables, and optimize space via 1D reverse-capacity sweeps.

title: Unbounded Knapsack & Coin Change Combinations
learning_objectives: Implement unbounded knapsack choices where items can be selected repeatedly via forward loops
Differentiate Coin Change 1 (minimum coins) from Coin Change 2 (combination ways)
description: Solve Unbounded Knapsack and Coin Change (min coins and combinations count) using 1D forward capacity loops in O(N * W) time.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence (O(N log N))
concepts: Patience Sorting & Tails Array O(N log N)
learning_objectives: Formulate the standard O(N^2) LIS recurrence checking all predecessor indices
Optimize LIS to O(N log N) time using Patience Sorting and bisect binary search over tails arrays
description: Optimize Longest Increasing Subsequence from O(N^2) DP to O(N log N) using patience sorting and binary search.

title: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS)
learning_objectives: Construct a 2D LCS matrix tracking character matches and max diagonal transitions
Reconstruct the optimal subsequence string by backtracking through the DP table in O(M * N) time
description: Implement Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) for two strings, formulate 2D transitions, and reconstruct alignments.

title: Edit Distance (Levenshtein Distance)
learning_objectives: Formulate the Levenshtein distance recurrence evaluating insert, delete, and substitute costs
Compute minimum edit operations to transform word1 into word2 in O(M * N) time
description: Compute the Levenshtein Edit Distance between two strings with insertion, deletion, and replacement operations in O(M*N) time.

title: Interval DP: Matrix Chain & Burst Balloons
learning_objectives: Solve optimization problems over contiguous intervals by iterating span lengths
Solve Burst Balloons by choosing which balloon bursts last within interval (i, j)
description: Master Interval DP by iterating over subarray lengths, formulating boundary transitions (Burst Balloons, Matrix Chain).

title: Section 13 Review & Multi-State DP Design
learning_objectives: Architect state-machine DP models tracking multiple simultaneous states (e.g. stock trading with cooldowns)
Select optimal state representations and recurrence orders across all DP archetypes
description: Synthesize 1D, 2D, knapsack, subsequence, interval, and state-machine DP patterns into a comprehensive DP master class.

title: Bit Manipulation, Bitmasks & Brian Kernighan
learning_objectives: Clear the lowest set bit in O(1) operations using n & (n - 1) to count set bits
Represent subsets and visited states compactly using integer bitmasks (1 << i)
description: Master bitwise operations, Brian Kernighan's algorithm, power-of-two tests, and subset generation with bitmasks.

title: Backtracking & State-Space Pruning (N-Queens)
learning_objectives: Implement complete backtracking frameworks with choose, explore, and unchoose steps
Prune invalid search branches in N-Queens using column and diagonal bitmask sets
description: Implement systematic backtracking with search-space pruning, bitmask tracking, and solve the N-Queens problem.

title: Segment Trees & Fenwick Trees Primer
concepts: O(log N) Range Query & Point Update
learning_objectives: Construct flat array-based Segment Trees supporting logarithmic range queries and point updates
Differentiate Segment Trees from Binary Indexed Trees (Fenwick Trees) for range computations
description: Build array-based Segment Trees and Fenwick Trees supporting O(log N) range queries and point updates.

title: Complex Problem Decomposition & System Design
learning_objectives: Deconstruct ambiguous multi-faceted problems into clear data structure and algorithm pipelines
Design a rate limiter and cache eviction system meeting production scale constraints
description: Decompose complex end-to-end coding interview challenges into interconnected DS/algorithm components.

title: The 160-Day Capstone: Interview Readiness
learning_objectives: Demonstrate full fluency across Python fundamentals, memory models, data structures, and algorithms
Complete the final capstone assessment simulating a rigorous technical interview loop
description: Complete the comprehensive 160-day curriculum capstone, demonstrating complete technical mastery from Python foundations to advanced DSA.
